description: For spec PRs, open the source ticket the change came from (id in the branch name or `proposal.md` Traceability) if the project uses a tracker. Check its description for a `Scope narrowed` footer. If absent, judge the CURRENT description against the `managing-openspec` skill's TRIAGE topic heuristics: one change, one shippable outcome. Flag CRITICAL when the ticket plainly covers several independent outcomes that should have been split before speccing. If the footer is present (sibling tickets were created), the PR MUST target only that narrowed scope, never scope that moved to a sibling; flag CRITICAL otherwise. SKIP with evidence when the change has no source ticket.

`openspec/config.yaml` must declare a `schema:` naming a schema the project actually ships (see the `schemas/` directory the project installed, e.g. `booster-mvp` or `booster-standard`). Flag a missing `schema:` key, or one naming a schema that does not exist on disk.
Verify `proposal.md` has all required sections: Why, What Changes, Affected Boundaries, Non-Goals, Capabilities, Traceability.
Verify `design.md` (when present) has required sections: Scope (MUST/MUST NOT/NICE TO HAVE), Decisions, Risks.
Every requirement must have at least one scenario.
Every ADDED or MODIFIED requirement must have at least one non-happy-path scenario.

Only applies to OpenSpec PRs — PRs that include changed files under `openspec/changes/`. If `tasks.md` is absent from such a PR, flag it as critical. Skip this check entirely for ad-hoc `fix`, `feat`, `chore`, or `refactor` PRs that contain no `openspec/changes/` files — those do not go through the OpenSpec process and are not required to have a tasks.md.

`tasks.md` must contain every numbered section its schema defines, with no gaps: sections 1-9 on `booster-standard` (1 `[contracts+db]`, 2 `[api]`, 3 `[worker]`, 4 `[web]`, 5 `[e2e-tests]`, 6 `[local-checks]`, 7 `[browser-qa]`, 8 `[ship]`, 9 `[librarian]`) and sections 1-6 on `booster-mvp`. Read the schema named in `openspec/config.yaml` before judging — never assume a section count. Conditional sections (`[worker]`, `[e2e-tests]`, `[browser-qa]`) stay in the file with an `N/A` body when they do not apply; they are never deleted. Flag any missing section heading.

On `booster-standard`, `tasks.md` must contain `[local-checks]` (section 6) with exactly 1 task, `[browser-qa]` (section 7), `[ship]` (section 8) with exactly 3 tasks (spec-coverage plus archive, client docs, then open PR and merge), and `[librarian]` as the last section (section 9) with exactly 1 task. Flag a local `[review]` section: code review runs in CI when the PR opens, so a local one duplicates it. Read the schema named in `openspec/config.yaml` first and check against that schema's lifecycle sections — `booster-mvp` collapses the same lifecycle into fewer sections and fewer tasks.
Each implementation task in boundary sections (`[contracts+db]`, `[api]`, `[worker]`, `[web]`) and the `[e2e-tests]` section must have Accepts-when, Test-first, and Spec-scenarios sub-fields.

If the PR adds or modifies runtime code that introduces new user-facing behavior, verify `docs/features/<feature>/README.md` exists and is updated. On spec-only PRs, only flag if a new capability directory is added under `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` with no corresponding feature doc update.
If `docs/features/<feature>/README.md` is modified or created, verify a corresponding row exists in `docs/FEATURES.md`.
Capabilities listed in `proposal.md` must match the directories present under `specs/`. Flag any capability listed but missing as a directory, or any directory present but not listed.
Affected boundaries listed in `proposal.md` must match the boundary sections present in `tasks.md`. Flag mismatches.
`[e2e-tests]` section must contain tasks (not `N/A`) when functional boundaries (api, worker, or web) exist.
`[browser-qa]` section must contain tasks (not `N/A`) when functional boundaries exist AND `[web]` tasks are present.
Design decisions referenced in `tasks.md` Context fields must exist in `design.md`. Flag references to decisions not defined there.
Factual claims about the codebase in `design.md` (file paths, line numbers, function names) should be spot-checked against actual files. Flag claims that are demonstrably wrong.

If code CHANGES existing routes, service methods, or BullMQ jobs (modifying previously documented behavior), verify the corresponding `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` still reflects reality. Only flag when: (1) a spec already exists for that capability AND (2) the existing spec now contradicts the new code. Do NOT flag when code adds entirely new behavior for which no spec yet exists — spec creation for new features is a separate OpenSpec process tracked by ClickUp, not a blocking concern for this PR. SKIP when the project does not use queue-backed jobs.

If an `AGENTS.md` file adds or changes a convention that reviewers should enforce (e.g., banned imports, required patterns, file placement rules), check whether the corresponding code-reviewing domain file already covers it. If not, flag as warning: the code-reviewing skill needs updating to include the new rule.

When an `AGENTS.md` or `AGENT.md` file changes, flag descriptive openers like `This package provides...`, `The module is...`, `This document describes...`, or long why/prose blocks before any directive. AGENTS files must open with an imperative directive, `When you need ...`, or a `MUST` constraint. Fix guidance: Load `editing-markdown-docs` before editing the file (it is the authority for all agent-facing markdown, including AGENTS.md).

When an `AGENTS.md` or `AGENT.md` file changes, flag generic table headers like `Description`, `Purpose`, or `Details`. AGENTS tables must answer `when` or `what to copy` using headers like `When to use`, `When to modify`, `Copy from`, or `Configuration`. Fix guidance: Load `editing-markdown-docs` before editing the file.

When an `AGENTS.md` or `AGENT.md` file changes, flag sections that explain a reference, pattern, or file group without telling the agent when to use it, copy from it, or modify it. AGENTS content must be operational, not explanatory. Prefer `When you need ...` tables and constraint-framed bullets (`**Entity** — short. MUST ...`). Fix guidance: Load `editing-markdown-docs` before editing the file.

When the diff changes Markdown that instructs an agent — `AGENTS.md`, `AGENT.md`, any `SKILL.md` or bundled skill topic file, `.ai/docs/*.md`, `.ai/lessons.md`, or a skill/package `README.md` — load the `editing-markdown-docs` skill and read the topics its routing table maps to the changed files (`WRITING.md` for prose, `STRUCTURING.md` for skill structure, `PATTERNS.md` for large or router documents), then judge the diff against them. Flag: (1) a rule stated in the diff that another file in the repo already owns — one authoritative owner per rule, link instead of restating it; (2) any project-specific path, command, permission, filename, or skill name asserted in the diff that does not resolve in this repository; (3) a document that grew past the skill's size guidance without being split into topics. Tone and table-header rules for AGENTS files are covered by the `agents-*` rules — do not re-report those here. SKIP when no agent-facing Markdown changed.

When a `SKILL.md` changes, load `editing-markdown-docs` (`STRUCTURING.md` plus `WRITING.md`) and check the frontmatter and shape against them: `name` matches the skill's directory name; `description` leads with `Use when ...`, is written in third person, and packs trigger keywords; `description` does NOT summarize the skill's workflow or process steps, since agents then follow the summary and never read the body; `metadata.version` is bumped in the same diff as any body change; the body carries no `When to Use` section (the body loads only after the skill triggers); and bundled resources live inside the skill's own directory. SKIP when no `SKILL.md` changed.

When the diff renames or deletes a skill directory, a bundled skill topic file, an agent file, or a command file, sweep the whole repository for the old name and flag every surviving reference. Check at minimum: permission allow-lists (`opencode.json`), lockfiles, other skills' bodies and routing tables, agent and command prompts, active OpenSpec artifacts under `openspec/changes/`, schema and config templates, validator or check scripts, CI workflows, and `AGENTS.md` routing rows. Cite each surviving reference as `path:line`. A dangling skill name is silent: the router never loads the skill and the agent proceeds without the instructions the reference promised. SKIP when the diff renames and deletes nothing.

For spec PRs (any changed file under `openspec/changes/`): load the project's testing-conventions skill, if one exists, and the `AGENTS.md` of every package in `proposal.md` Affected Boundaries. Apply the value gate ('Would this catch a bug that types or the library's own tests do not?') to every `spec.md` scenario and every `tasks.md` Test-first path. Flag scenarios or test files that exercise framework/library behavior (NOT NULL, FK existence, pgEnum, Drizzle insert/select, NestJS routing, passthrough `*.controller.spec.ts` alongside service spec, Zod built-ins per the project's testing-conventions Zod table, if one exists) or violate per-package `AGENTS.md` test conventions. Propose a replacement scenario when one exists (custom CHECK constraints, non-trivial query joins, `.refine()` / `.transform()` / `discriminatedUnion`, business logic). If no `openspec/changes/` files changed, submit pass with evidence 'SKIP: not a spec PR'.

If the PR removes, skips, marks `continue-on-error`, or otherwise weakens `task openspec:check`, `scripts/check-openspec.mjs`, or `openspec validate --all`, flag as critical. Deterministic OpenSpec checks must stay automated and blocking.

If the PR changes a schema's archive task-generation instructions (`[ship]` task 8.1 on `booster-standard`) and removes the requirement to run the project's OpenSpec validation command against the change id after archiving, flag as critical. Archive without validation lets a malformed change sync into the canonical specs.

For PRs that directly edit `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` without touching any `openspec/changes/<name>/` directory (lightweight single-PR spec-linked changes per the `managing-openspec` skill's MINOR-CHANGES.md topic): verify (1) the canonical spec edit is internally consistent — scenario headings use `####`, requirements use `### Requirement:`, every scenario has GIVEN/WHEN/THEN and a `**Test boundary:**` line; (2) the implementation and tests in the same PR cover all changed or added scenarios; (3) `task openspec:check` was stated as passing; (4) if user-visible web behavior changed, browser QA result is mentioned. Do not flag for absent `openspec/changes/` artifacts, `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, or archive directory — these are intentionally omitted in this lane. If no `openspec/specs/` file was modified, submit pass with evidence 'SKIP: no canonical spec edited'.

SKIP unless the repo has `docs/qa/config.json` and the diff adds or modifies a scenario file under the directory its `scenarios` key names. Judge each changed scenario against the `managing-qa-scenarios` skill's SCENARIOS.md topic, checking only what its `check-qa.mjs` script cannot: (1) it covers exactly one user goal; (2) it follows a business-critical path across several screens or roles, not single-screen CRUD or a settings toggle; (3) `What can go wrong` names real failure modes this scenario would catch, not generic risks; (4) every step is an action a real user takes in the UI; (5) preconditions create their own fixtures and depend on no hardcoded IDs. Do NOT re-check section structure, frontmatter enums, IDs, selectors, or bold UI labels; the script owns those.
